_comment: SAMPLE CONTENT — PROTOTYPE ONLY. Not authoritative, not steward-approved. The Ministry of Interior civil registration domain is the Phase 1 flagship (recommendation on OD-01); these chunks exist so the pipeline can be exercised against a second ministry and cross-ministry life-event bundles before onboarding begins.

chunks.text: Registration of a birth is made at the commune or sangkat administration of the place where the birth occurred, within thirty days of the birth. The declarant submits the hospital birth notification, the family book, and the identity documents of both parents. The commune clerk issues the birth certificate on the same working day where the file is complete.

chunks.text: Where a birth was not registered within the prescribed period, late registration is permitted. The declarant submits two witness statements from persons resident in the commune, together with any available supporting documents such as a hospital record, a vaccination record, or a school record. Late registration files are reviewed by the commune chief before the certificate is issued.

chunks.text: A birth occurring outside the Kingdom of Cambodia to a Cambodian parent is declared at the Cambodian embassy or consulate with jurisdiction over the place of birth. The declarant submits the foreign birth record with a certified translation, the passports of the parents, and evidence of Cambodian nationality of at least one parent. The record is transmitted to the Ministry of Interior for entry in the civil register.

chunks.text: An error in a name, date, or place recorded in the civil register is corrected on written request to the commune administration that holds the entry. The applicant submits the certificate containing the error, documentary evidence of the correct particulars, and the family book. A correction that alters a person's identity rather than a clerical error requires a court decision.

chunks.text: A death is declared at the commune or sangkat administration of the place where the death occurred, within fifteen days. The declarant submits the medical certificate of death or, where the death occurred outside a health facility, a statement certified by the local authority, together with the identity documents of the deceased and the family book. The commune clerk issues the death certificate and updates the family book.

chunks.text: The family book records the members of a household and is issued by the commune or sangkat administration of residence. The book is updated on birth, death, marriage, divorce, and change of residence. The head of household presents the existing book and the certificate evidencing the change. A household that moves to another commune surrenders the book at the former commune and is issued a new book at the commune of new residence.

chunks.text: Registration of a birth within the prescribed period and issue of the first birth certificate are provided at the fee set in this annex, which in this prototype is a placeholder and must not be relied upon. Subsequent copies, late registration, and corrections carry the separate fees set in the annex. Payment is made at the commune administration against an official receipt. No payment may be required by any person other than the responsible clerk.

chunks.doc: [SAMPLE] Rights of Applicants at Civil Registration Offices
chunks.text: An applicant is entitled to be informed of the documents required, the applicable fee, and the processing time before submitting a file. Where a file is refused, the applicant is entitled to a written statement of the reason for refusal. An applicant who considers that a file has been wrongly refused, or that a payment has been required beyond the published fee, may raise the matter with the district administration and thereafter with the provincial administration.
